items.title: RM6.7m boost for Indian community
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Putrajaya has allocated RM6.7 million under the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit to empower the Indian community through education, entrepreneurship and support for religious institutions. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the Madani Tuition Programme, Uyarvu Madani and Dharma Madani are important initiatives for the community's holistic development and economic growth. Ramanan said 91 entrepreneurs received grants under the Micro category, 29 under Growth and eight under High Growth.

items.title: Malaysia targets RM85.2bil energy savings by 2035 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia expects its National Energy Efficiency Action Plan 2026-2035 (NEEAP 2.0) to generate RM85.24 billion in cumulative utility savings by 2035, as it seeks to contain energy demand amid rapid industrial expansion and the shift to cleaner power. The plan targets an 11.6 per cent reduction in national energy demand, equivalent to cumulative energy savings of 815,382 terajoules (TJ) against a business-as-usual scenario, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said. NEEAP 2.0 complements the National Energy Policy 2022-2040, the National Energy Transition Roadmap, the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and the 12th and 13th Malaysia Plans.

items.title: Of MMC Ports, Strait of Malacca and Sultan Ahmed's appointment
items.summary: MMC Port Holdings Bhd (MMC Ports) now operates the country's largest port network, which handled more than 20 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in 2025. The group subsequently built a network encompassing Johor Port, Northport in Port Klang, Penang Port and Tanjung Bruas Port. Today, MMC Ports operates PTP, Northport, Johor Port, Penang Port, Tanjung Bruas Port, Andaman Port, Port Klang Cruise Terminal and Langkawi Cruise Terminal.

items.title: Car bomb kills Haftar intel chief in Libya
items.summary: TRIPOLI: The head of military intelligence for the Libyan National Army (LNA), which controls the east and parts of southern Libya, has been killed in a car bombing, the army said in a statement Tuesday. Reports said the killing occurred in the eastern Libyan city of Benghazi. Two governments are currently vying for power: the UN-recognised administration in Tripoli led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah, and a rival in Benghazi backed by military commander and LNA chief Khalifa Haftar.

items.title: Total solar eclipse to spellbind Europe
items.summary: BURGOS, Spain: Millions of Europeans will contemplate the sky in awe on Wednesday as a rare total solar eclipse crosses part of the continent and plunges a swathe of Spain into eerie daytime darkness. In Spain, where the total eclipse will be best viewed, the shadow will cross the country diagonally from the northern Atlantic coast to the Mediterranean Sea, where it will vanish at around 1830 GMT. This will be mainland Europe's first total eclipse since 2006.

items.title: Access to justice: Reflections from a mobile court
items.summary: The gravel road alone clocked 8km. Inside the community hall, tables for various government agencies coordinated under the judiciary's initiative were hastily arranged, including, among others, the National Registration Department, Attorney-General's Chambers, Legal Aid Department and Welfare Department, bringing vital assistance directly to the door-step of people who rarely see it. It was the people.

items.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile over Sea of Japan
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korea fired a ballistic missile off its east coast towards Japan early Wednesday, Seoul's military said, just days before the planned start of massive US-South Korea joint drills. "Our military detected at around 6am (2100 GMT Tuesday) a ballistic missile launched by North Korea from the Wonsan area towards the East Sea," the Joint Chiefs of Staff said in a message to reporters, referring to a body of water also known as the Sea of Japan. Japan's Defence Ministry said on social media that the suspected ballistic missile had "already fallen", without providing further details.

items.title: SWCorp investigates alleged Singapore construction waste dumped in Pontian [WATCH]
items.summary: PONTIAN: Johor will set up a multi-agency task force to conduct a comprehensive investigation into allegations that construction waste from Singapore was dumped at several locations here. State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the task force would comprise local authorities, police, the district office and the Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Corporation (SWCorp). Jafni said any waste brought in from Singapore and dumped in Johor without the necessary permits or approvals should not be allowed.

items.title: Explained: Kedah’s bid to stop lotteries reaches Federal Court today; here’s what it’s about
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Kedah state government is asking the Federal Court today to allow it to proceed with its appeals, with the ultimate goal of stopping lotteries from operating in the state. Previously on December 12, 2025, the Court of Appeal had in a 2-1 decision said the Kedah state government had acted unconstitutionally, unlawfully and irrationally when it decided to not renew the physical outlets’ premises licences for these lotteries starting from 2023. The Kedah state government wants to appeal this, but it has to first get leave or permission from the Federal Court for the appeal to be heard.

items.title: Trump smuggled off Air Force One in secret Iran threat escape
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A secret operation that reportedly smuggled Donald Trump off Air Force One in a catering truck before the plane departed carrying journalists and top aides at apparent risk of an Iranian strike has raised questions over US security practices. But he then reportedly quickly left the plane, stepping inside one of the cargo containers, to board a smaller US Air Force aircraft positioned nearby. - SHOULDER-TO-AIR MISSILE THREAT?

items.title: 'Zombie city': Pereira reels from quake that killed 240
items.summary: PEREIRA, Colombia: Jorge Gonzalez searches with his bare hands for his aunt under the ruins of a four-story building in Pereira, one of the cities hardest hit by the powerful earthquake in Colombia that has left at least 240 dead. Like hundreds of volunteers and rescuers, he has spent hours clinging to the faintest hope there may be survivors in the rubble, despite the 7.4 magnitude quake that struck this coffee capital on Monday morning. "Since yesterday, I got here and I haven't left.

items.title: US, allies warn against unannounced missile launches
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The United States and some 40 other countries warned Tuesday of the dangers of ballistic missile testing without advance notice, in a joint statement issued a month after China launched a nuclear-capable missile in the Pacific. "Conducting nuclear-capable ballistic missile tests without sufficient advance notice and detail is dangerous and disrupts the peace and security of relevant nations in proximity to these tests," said the joint statement issued by countries from Europe and the Indo-Pacific. The statement called on all countries to provide at least 24 hours' notice of launches, including the class of missile being launched as well as the planned launch window, area and direction.

items.title: US helicopter fired on ship that tried to break Iran ports blockade
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A US helicopter on Tuesday fired missiles into the engine room of a Panama-flagged cargo ship that attempted to break the American blockade of Iran's ports, the United States military said. The US Navy MH-60 helicopter fired on and disabled the M/V Vela Nova "after the ship's civilian crew ignored repeated warnings from American forces," US Central Command (CENTCOM) said on X, adding that the vessel "is no longer transiting to Iran in violation of the US blockade." It was the third time the United States, in a months-long war against Iran, has forcibly halted a vessel since reinstating the ports blockade on July 14.

items.title: Taiwan's return to summit triggers Beijing warning
items.summary: China warned a top Pacific Islands diplomat to "avoid affecting the healthy and stable development of ties" yesterday, after he said Taiwan would attend an annual meeting of the regional bloc's leaders. The island was barred from the Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting last year after protests from Beijing, which claims Taiwan as part of its territory. Baron Waqa, the forum's secretary-general, said last Friday Taipei would attend this year.

items.title: Aratas invests RM259m in advanced manufacturing facility
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Aratas Corp, a member of the Omron Group, is investing about RM259 million to build an advanced manufacturing facility at COMPASS @ Kota Seri Langat, Selangor, as it expands production capacity to meet growing demand in India and the Asia-Pacific region. Omron Malaysia Sdn Bhd, Aratas' manufacturing arm, selected the 6.87ha site after signing a sale and purchase agreement with COMPASS IP Sdn Bhd. COMPASS is a joint venture between Permodalan Nasional Bhd, Area Group and KWEST Group.

items.title: Syed Saddiq: Don't burden future generations with fund's rescue
items.summary: The financial burden of rescuing Tabung Haji must not be passed on to future generations and taxpayers, said Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar). We are boycotting our duty to millions of Tabung Haji depositors." While agreeing that Anwar should respond to criticism over the government's handling of the Tabung Haji report and its recovery plan upon returning to Parliament, Syed Saddiq said his absence should not stall proceedings.

items.title: Malaysia steps up connectivity push
items.summary: Malaysia is positioning itself as a more connected regional economy, with the expanded air links and its multiple growth corridors aimed at attracting investment from Hong Kong and beyond. He said Kuala Lumpur and Hong Kong were less than four hours apart by air and shared the same time zone, with Cathay Pacific operating four daily services between the cities since March. That tells us the commercial demand is growing," he said at the Think Business, Think Hong Kong symposium here yesterday.

items.title: Air India captain's confirmatory drug test positive for marijuana, source says
items.summary: NEW DELHI: The captain of an Air India Phuket-Delhi flight that suddenly lost about 91.44 metres (300 feet) of altitude last week has tested positive for marijuana in a confirmatory drug test, a source familiar with the matter said. Earlier in the day, India's Ministry of Civil Aviation summoned Air India CEO Campbell Wilson over the incident, which involved an Airbus A320neo aircraft, a second source said. Air India and the ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

items.title: US rights groups sue Trump over ICC sanctions
items.summary: NEW YORK: Rights groups on Tuesday sued US President Donald Trump over his sanctions targeting the International Criminal Court, saying the measures block victims of war crimes from pursuing justice. The US sanctions, issued under an executive order Trump signed in February 2025, have targeted eight judges, three prosecutors, a UN expert and three human rights organizations. US reservations about the court predate Trump.

items.title: Assad ruled Syria with iron fist before defeat in civil war
items.summary: Assad became president in 2000 after the death of his father, Hafez. Following one poison gas attack in 2018, then-US President Donald Trump declared Assad an "animal." Authorities denied using chemical weapons, which killed and injured thousands during the war.

items.title: Ocalan is founder of Kurdish PKK and also author of its end
items.summary: ABDULLAH Ocalan, jailed founder of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) and an icon for many Kurds but a reviled terrorist for many Turks, is now at the heart of the biggest push for peace in over a decade. Since the latest tentative moves began in October 2024, PKK leaders demanded Ocalan's release as essential for the process to work. For many Turks, Ocalan, who founded the PKK in 1978 and embodies the Kurdish rebellion, is the No.

items.title: 'Spirit of Anchorage' a shadow of itself one year after summit
items.summary: TRUMP-PUTIN TALKS IN the year since Donald Trump hosted Vladimir Putin in the United States for a summit designed to broker an end to Russia's offensive on Ukraine, the diplomatic initiative has fizzled out and the conflict has escalated. US mediation efforts are at a standstill, Russia and Ukraine are ramping up attacks and more civilians are being killed than at any point since the first months of the war. Russia has always maintained some kind of understanding that a peace deal was struck — "a compromise proposal", as Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov called it.

items.title: Man arrested over alleged machete robbery of elderly woman in Ipoh
items.summary: IPOH: A 32-year-old man has been arrested for allegedly robbing an elderly woman at a house in Langkap near Teluk Intan. Hilir Perak District Police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said police received a report from the 69-year-old woman, who claimed she had been robbed by an unidentified man. "Police also recovered and seized a gold bracelet believed to be linked to the case for further investigation," he said in a statement tonight.

items.title: Two 14-year-old boys feared drowned while swimming in river
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Two 14-year-old boys are feared drowned while swimming in a river at Kampung Batu Lada Aur Duri, Kuala Krai, today. A spokesperson for the Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre said the department received a distress call at 6.39pm and firefighters from the Kuala Krai Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene, arriving at 6.46pm. "The operation, involving seven personnel from the Kuala Krai, was hampered by heavy rain when firefighters arrived at the scene.

items.title: NST Leader: Housing policies must put people before numbers
items.summary: THE government deserves credit for moving beyond merely announcing new projects and addressing the legacy problem of abandoned developments. For decades, stalled projects have scarred communities and left buyers financially and emotionally burdened. Data-driven planning must remain central to housing, not developers' or policymakers' whims and fancies.

items.title: No by-election for Subang after Wong Chen's resignation - EC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: No by-election will be held for the Subang parliamentary seat following the resignation of PKR's Wong Chen as its MP, the Election Commission (EC) confirmed. In a statement posted on Facebook, EC chairman Datuk Sri Ramlan Harun said the commission was notified about the seat's vacancy by Dewan Rakyat Speaker Johari Abdul yesterday. Earlier today, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul notified the EC of the vacancy of the Subang parliamentary.

items.title: TH recovers bonuses paid to Properties board members [WATCH]
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the recovery was among the recommendations already implemented, accounting for 75 per cent of the RCI's recommendations. Winding up the debate on the RCI report in the Dewan Rakyat today, he said the RCI had also identified weaknesses in the valuation and financial reporting methods used to determine TH's financial position from 2014 to 2017. Zulkifli said the RCI's findings had subsequently formed the basis for strengthening internal controls, financial reporting and accountability within TH.

items.title: 5 Bank Negara warning letters on Tabung Haji to be referred to PM, cabinet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Proposals to release five Bank Negara Malaysia warning letters and other documents linked to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji will be referred to the prime minister and cabinet. The documents sought included five warning letters issued by Bank Negara to Tabung Haji, the Roland Berger report, minutes of meetings concerning changes to impairment policies and minutes relating to the approval of hibah distributions. KW: Tabung Haji, RCI, Bank Negara, Zulkifli Hasan, warning letters, Roland Berger, Dewan Rakyat, governance, Nst, News, Malaysia © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: RMAF, IAF test interoperability in Udara Shakti 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian and Indian fighter jets are taking part in a five-day air exercise aimed at improving interoperability between the two air forces. The Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) has deployed Sukhoi Su-30MKMs and F/A-18D Hornets, while the Indian Air Force (IAF) is taking part with Dassault Rafales in Exercise Udara Shakti 2026 (US 26). The exercise began yesterday and runs until Friday, with 83 officers and personnel from both air forces involved.

items.title: Aug 21 not a public holiday in Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA: There will be no public holiday in Melaka on Aug 21, as the date is not listed in the state's 2026 Public Holiday Schedule and no occasional holiday has been declared. State secretary Datuk Salhah Salleh said a clarification had been issued to dispel public confusion over Aug 21 (Friday), which has been linked to Melaka's Unesco World Heritage recognition. At the same time, Salleh said the state government remained committed to preserving and promoting Melaka's historical, cultural and heritage assets recognised as Unesco World Heritage Sites.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Tuesday, Aug 11, 2026
items.summary: NSTP/NABILA ADLINA AZAHARI [[nid:1509119]] KUALA LUMPUR – The Visit Malaysia 2026 logo featured at the KLCC grounds. NSTP/NABILA ADLINA AZAHARI [[nid:1509118]] KUALA LUMPUR – Contractors carry out cleaning work at the Parliament office building. NSTP/MOHD FADLI HAMZAH [[nid:1509114]] KUALA LUMPUR – Hazy conditions blanket Kuala Lumpur at 8.30am.

items.title: Beyond rockets: MYSA wants Malaysians to see how space tech shapes daily life
items.summary: Malaysian Space Agency (MYSA) director-general Datuk Azlikamil Napiah said the ‘Space for All’ aspiration means that space technology should be accessible, understood and utilised by all segments of society. “My aspiration is to see space technology brought closer to the people. He said space technology is not limited to observing outer space, but also helps humans manage life and resources on Earth through advanced systems such as communication satellites, navigation and remote sensing.

items.title: Finance Minister II: Seven of Tabung Haji’s 14 troubled investments ended in total losses, Saudi-based deal caused biggest hit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Seven of the 14 troubled investments involving Tabung Haji identified by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) resulted in total losses, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan told the Dewan Rakyat today. Amir Hamzah said that among the seven, investments linked to Saudi Arabia-based property development and management firm Al-Rawda Real Estates Development recorded the highest losses. “Al-Rawda began defaulting on its rent payments for Tabung Haji since the first quarter of 2019, leading to RM1.86 billion in losses as of 2024,” Amir Hamzah said during his winding-up speech on the Tabung Haji RCI report today.

items.title: ‘Let’s work together’: Sabah Fire Dept urges public to avoid open burning amid transboundary haze
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 11 — The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) has urged the public to stop open burning as transboundary haze from Kalimantan, Indonesia, has begun to affect air quality in the state. Its director Mohd Pisar Aziz said haze had begun to cover areas including Kota Kinabalu and Kimanis following forest fires in the neighbouring region. “Winds from southern and central Borneo are carrying thick smoke towards northern Borneo, affecting visibility and air quality in Sabah.

items.title: Former High Court judge’s driver jailed three after pleading guilty to criminal intimidation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The former driver of a Kuala Lumpur High Court judge was sentenced to three months’ jail by the Magistrate’s Court here today for criminally intimidating the judge last May. Magistrate Heng Yi Min handed down the sentence after Mohd Fareez Mohd Zin, 39, changed his plea to guilty during today’s case mention. According to the charge, he is accused of committing the offence against High Court Judge Gan Techiong, 64, with the intention of causing fear and alarm to the judge at the Kuala Lumpur High Court (Civil) complex, Jalan Duta, here, at 1.30pm on May 8.

items.title: RoS to scrutinise Bersatu complaint over Perikatan membership status
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 11 — The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) has confirmed receiving an official complaint from Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) over claims that the party was not involved in the Perikatan Nasional (PN) Supreme Council meeting on July 16 and issues related to its membership in the coalition. RoS said in a statement today that it was examining the complaint received today, based on the Societies Act 1966 [Act 832], the Societies Regulations 1984, the organisation's approved constitution, and the department's official records. RoS also stressed that every registered organisation must comply with the Societies Act 1966, relevant regulations and its respective constitution.

items.title: Police bust syndicate storing RM21m worth of ganja near KLIA, Penang airport
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 11 — Federal narcotics police foiled an international drug syndicate’s tactic of storing ganja flowers supplied from neighbouring countries at residences near international airports before they were transported by drug mules, following the arrest of nine individuals earlier this month. “The syndicate’s modus operandi was to temporarily store the ganja flowers obtained via our northern neighbour at terrace houses near Penang International Airport in Bayan Lepas and Kuala Lumpur International Airport near Nilai, Negeri Sembilan. Following the initial raid, police arrested six more suspects around Sepang, Selangor, and Bayan Lepas on August 3, seizing an additional 60 packages of ganja flowers.

items.title: Drug smuggling via KLIA: 14 Malaysians arrested abroad since January, say police
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 11 — A total of 14 Malaysians have been arrested overseas for alleged drug smuggling activities after departing on outbound flights from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) between January and July this year, federal narcotics police said today. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Commissioner Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the 14 Malaysians comprised 11 men and three women, with Taiwan recording the highest number of arrests at six. In contrast, Hussein said federal police successfully thwarted drug smuggling activities at KLIA during the same period, arresting 51 individuals and seizing a total of 1.2 tonnes of drugs worth RM97 million.

items.title: Five motorcycles seized after man repeatedly caught for extreme modifications
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The actions of a man who spent up to RM25,000 to extremely modify five motorcycles backfired when all the vehicles were confiscated by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) after he was detained five times since last year. JPJ Senior Director of Enforcement Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said the fifth motorcycle belonging to the self-employed man was detained during JPJ’s Op Ekstrem around the capital recently for offences involving the modification of engine structures, braking systems, and the use of components not complying with safety specifications. He said that throughout Op Ekstrem conducted on August 8 and 9, a total of 443 motorcycles were inspected, with 336 of them acted against and 140 motorcycles confiscated.

items.title: Muhyiddin urges govt to complete forensic audit of Tabung Haji funds within a year
items.summary: The former prime minister said the move was important following weaknesses in governance and transparency in the management of TH funds, as revealed in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution. “Anyone responsible for causing losses to TH funds, whether through fraud, abuse of power or negligence, must be brought to justice,” he said during the debate on the TH RCI report at the Special Dewan Rakyat Sitting today. Meanwhile, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (MUDA-Muar) urged the government to establish a Multi-Agency Task Force to investigate 14 problematic TH investments identified in the RCI report.

items.title: Bukit Aman sends narcotics team to Jakarta to question Malaysian pilot held with 26kg ecstasy
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 11 — A team of officers from the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department has arrived in Indonesia to question a Malaysian pilot arrested with drugs at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport last month. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Commissioner Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the team of four arrived earlier today and has been given two days, August 12 to 13, to interrogate the suspect. Hussein said investigators were tracing the alleged syndicate members but faced some difficulties because the phone numbers used for communication were registered under false or inaccurate identities.

items.title: Police detain eight over suspected murder of man at Kuala Langat oil palm plantation
items.summary: KUALA LANGAT, Aug 11 — Police are investigating the death of a man believed to have been murdered at an oil palm plantation in Sungai Kelambu, Banting here last Sunday. Kuala Langat District Police chief Supt Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi, in a statement, said eight individuals had been arrested to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code. Akmalrizal also urged members of the public with information to go to the nearest police station or contact the Kuala Langat District Police Headquarters Operations Room at 03-3187 2222.

items.title: IGP: Police officers must keep evolving as security landscape grows more dynamic
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has urged all police officers to think critically, act swiftly and remain relevant amid changing times to meet the challenges of an increasingly dynamic policing landscape. “Promotion is not the pinnacle of a career, but rather the starting point of far greater and more challenging responsibilities,” he said at the Police Senior Officers’ Rank Insignia and Honorary Rank Insignia Presentation Ceremony at the Senior Police Officers’ Mess, Bukit Aman here today. A total of 29 senior police officers were honoured at the ceremony for their promotions to the ranks of Commissioner of Police (CP), Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Senior Assistant Commissioner (SAC) and Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP).

items.title: Johor police bust drug syndicate supplying local market, seize RM8.49m worth of drugs
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 11 — Johor police have busted a drug trafficking syndicate following the arrest of two men and the seizure of various types of drugs worth RM8.49 million in two separate raids in the Seri Alam area here on Wednesday (Aug 5). Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the raids were conducted at an apartment in Masai and a terrace house in Taman Ehsan Jaya at about 10.30 am. “Upon inspecting the apartment, we seized 132,600 Erimin 5 pills, 53,000 ecstasy pills, 290 packets of ecstasy powder, 13 packets of ketamine and two packets of Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) powder, weighing 96.76 kg in total,” he told a press conference at the Johor Police Headquarters here today.

items.title: PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim says lawyers handling Anwar’s defamation suit
items.summary: KOTA BARU, Aug 11 — PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said he would leave it to his lawyers to respond to the defamation suit filed against him by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The Kubang Kerian MP said the remarks at the centre of the suit were general in nature and had also been raised by other parties and sources, the New Straits Times reported. Anwar’s lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said the statements were false and defamatory of the Prime Minister.

items.title: Four-month-old baby girl’s death in Johor probed as murder, investigation papers sent to prosecution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Police have reclassified the death of a four-month-old baby girl in Taman Sri Saujana in Johor Bahru as murder, with the investigation papers referred to the Johor prosecution office for further action. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the investigation was initially conducted under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 for neglect resulting in the baby’s death, before being reclassified under Section 302 of the Penal Code following a post-mortem. He said the completed investigation papers were referred to the Johor prosecution office yesterday, while police had received instructions to charge the baby’s step-grandmother under Section 302 at the Kota Tinggi Magistrates’ Court tomorrow.

items.title: Sarawak orders schools to halt outdoor activities amid unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Schools in Sarawak have been ordered to immediately halt all outdoor activities involving pupils in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100. Sarawak Education Department director Omar Mahli said district education offices and educational institutions under the department had been reminded to prioritise the welfare, health and safety of pupils amid hot weather and haze, Utusan Malaysia reported today. “For areas recording API readings above 100, all outdoor activities involving pupils must be stopped,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Woman, 78, believed killed in crocodile attack while collecting river snails in Batu Niah
items.summary: The victim has been identified as Sambai Anggah. According to the Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba), Sambai and her 31-year-old daughter were searching for snails around a tributary connected to Sungai Suai when the incident occurred. Her daughter, who was in the river about one metre away, witnessed the crocodile snare Sambai from the boat.

items.title: Johor sets up special team to probe claims of Singapore waste dumped in Pontian
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 11 — The Johor government has set up a special team to investigate claims that construction waste from Singapore is illegally dumped in Pontian. Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the team was formed with an integrated approach to enable a comprehensive investigation into the allegations. Mohd Jafni was responding to claims that construction waste from Singapore had entered Johor and was dumped in Pontian.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI: MPs call for transparent probe, accountability to protect depositors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Members of Parliament across the political divide today called for independent and transparent investigations into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) after it was tabled in Parliament. Government backbenchers, led by Sekijang MP Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa, called on the government to clarify the involvement of TH’s leadership between 2014 and 2020 in negotiations over investments and allegations surrounding the matter. Dr Zaliha also called on the government to publish a complete report on the progress of the 25 recommendations made by the RCI to restore depositors’ confidence in TH.

items.title: Appeal backfires as man’s sentence for causing two-month-old daughter’s death raised to 30 years
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 11 — A man who appealed for a shorter prison sentence for causing the death of his two-month-old daughter instead had his sentence increased to the maximum 30 years by the Court of Appeal here today. Justice Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz, who delivered the decision of a three-member bench, said although the prosecution had not cross-appealed against the sentence, the court had the discretionary power under Section 60 of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 (CJA) to enhance Muhammad Daniel Iman Mohd Sharif’s sentence. Justice Hayatul said the 16-year prison sentence imposed by the Shah Alam High Court did not reflect the seriousness of the offence and the violence involved.

items.title: Man jailed two years for punching wife, attempting to murder her with car
items.summary: KANGAR, Aug 12 — A man was sentenced to two years in prison by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to injuring and attempting to murder his wife in September last year. Judge Sharifah Norazlita Syed Salim Idid sentenced Mohd Hasmi Mohd Salleh, 39, to one year in prison for intentionally causing hurt to his wife and two years for attempting to murder her, with the sentences to run concurrently from the date of his arrest on Sept 21, 2025. On the first charge, Mohd Hasmi was accused of punching his wife, Norzuraida Don Khodet, on her right arm, causing bruising.

items.title: Tabung Haji Act amendments to introduce tougher financial reporting rules, penalties
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan said the changes were intended to prevent a recurrence of the issues highlighted by the RCI in its report on TH management and operations from 2014 to 2020. “All relevant RCI recommendations have been reviewed for inclusion in the proposed amendments to the TH Act, including the suitability of a Securities Commission oversight and supervisory framework for TH’s fund management and investments,” he said when presenting his ministerial briefing on the RCI report at the special Dewan Rakyat sitting today. TH would remain a single, intact entity,” he said.

items.title: Johor orders Kempas scrap metal recycling premise to shut down over air pollution risk
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 11 — The Johor government has ordered an illegal scrap metal recycling premise in Kampung Maju Jaya, Kempas, here, to shut down immediately following claims of air pollution. The premise is also located near an underground gas pipeline owned by Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), raising safety concerns for more than 10,000 residents in four nearby villages. Also present were Johor Bahru Mayor Datuk Mohd Haffiz Ahmad, Johor Bahru North police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Ramdin Taha and Johor Solid Waste Management Corporation (SWCorp) director Zainal Fitri Ahmad.

items.title: Selangor seawater desalination plant feasibility study due by December
items.summary: State Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said Central Spectrum (M) Sdn Bhd, in collaboration with Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor), had appointed a consultant to conduct the study, which was expected to take six months. He said the study was among the state government’s efforts to diversify alternative water supply sources to meet development demands in the area, as well as reduce reliance on existing water treatment plants (LRAs). “Air Selangor projects that water supply demand will increase to 9,653 MLD by 2045.

items.title: Najib returned US$620m after GE13 because he was uncomfortable holding it, High Court told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The High Court here was told today that former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak returned US$620 million out of the US$681 million he received as a purported “Arab donation” because he was uncomfortable keeping such a large amount of money in his bank account. Najib’s lead counsel, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, said according to his client, the money was returned to the sender, Tanore Finance Corporation, after the 13th General Election (GE13) in 2013. The veteran lawyer said that Najib returned the money to Tanore in the hope that it (Tanore) was part of the Arab donation.

items.title: Make public full report on Tabung Haji RCI reforms, recovery efforts, says Dr Zaliha
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A full report on the implementation of the 25 recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), along with a report on efforts to recover its losses, should be made public to restore depositors’ confidence, Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa said. The Government Backbenchers Club (BBC) chairman and Sekijang MP said disclosure was important given TH’s role as a key institution for Malaysian Muslims, particularly in managing savings for the haj pilgrimage. The 211-page RCI report was only recently made public.

items.title: Seven-year-old Indonesian boy found drowned after falling into river in Subang Jaya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A seven-year-old Indonesian boy who fell into a river while playing with friends near Matahari Supermarket in Persiaran Subang Indah in Subang Jaya yesterday was found drowned this morning. The Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) said in a statement that the boy was found at 10.59am by personnel from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station and its Water Rescue Team (PPDA), Astro Awani reported. The search and rescue operation also involved PPDA personnel from the Shah Alam, Port Klang and KLIA fire and rescue stations, as well as personnel from the Puchong station.

items.title: Fix deadline for RCI reports to be tabled in Parliament, says Tuaran MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The Commissions of Enquiry Act 1950 should be amended to set a deadline for Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) reports to be tabled in Parliament, Tuaran MP Datuk Seri Wilfred Madius Tangau said today. Wilfred said the tabling of RCI reports should not be left solely to the government’s discretion as the purpose of establishing such commissions was to present the truth to the people. “So, the Commissions of Enquiry Act 1950 should be empowered so that tabling of RCI reports in Parliament does not rest solely on discretions (of the government),” Wilfred said during the debate on the Tabung Haji RCI report in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Kelantan opens 63 investigation papers into illegal mining, encroachment
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 11 — A total of 63 investigation papers were opened in connection with encroachment and illegal mining activities in Kelantan from 2025 to June this year. Kelantan Deputy Menteri Besar Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said the figure resulted from 77 enforcement operations conducted in hotspots involving the Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli and Tanah Merah districts. “The state government, through enforcement agencies, has intensified field action to curb such activities.
